findings.title: Optional[X] instead of X | None
findings.problem: code-quality.md Types And Imports requires X | None with from __future__ import annotations in new modules; the new module imports typing.Optional and declares auth_type, oauth_tenant_id, oauth_client_id, oauth_client_secret, ews_url, service_account_username, service_account_password as Optional[...], with no __future__ import.
findings.impact: A documented project code-quality standard is broken in newly added source; ruff's configured rule set (no UP/ANN) does not enforce it, so no gate catches it.
findings.recommendation: Add from __future__ import annotations, drop the typing.Optional import, and annotate the fields as ExchangeAuthType | None / str | None; confirm Pydantic still resolves the postponed annotations (run the ms_exchange model tests).

findings.title: Validator lacks return type annotation
findings.problem: code-quality.md requires explicit parameter and return types on new code; ExchangeToolConfig._validate_selected_path(self) has no return annotation.
findings.impact: Documented types standard unmet in new code; not covered by the configured ruff rules.
findings.recommendation: Annotate as def _validate_selected_path(self) -> ExchangeToolConfig (with postponed annotations) or -> Self.

findings.title: Whitespace-only path fields pass validation
findings.problem: _validate_selected_path checks selected-path fields with `if not getattr(self, name)`, so a whitespace-only ews_url, oauth_tenant_id, oauth_client_id, service_account_username or secret is accepted, while mailbox is checked with .strip().
findings.impact: A config with blank-looking credentials validates, contradicting AC4's intent that a missing selected-path field is rejected by name; the failure is deferred to connection time in future protocol code. No current backend caller constructs ExchangeToolConfig outside get_config, so the live consequence today is limited to that path.
findings.recommendation: Use the same check as mailbox: `if not (getattr(self, name) or "").strip(): raise ValueError(f"{name} is required when auth_type={self.auth_type.value}")`, and add whitespace cases to the both-path required-field tests.

findings.title: typing.List and untyped get_definition
findings.problem: code-quality.md prefers builtin generics and explicit return types in new code; toolkit.py imports typing.List for ExchangeToolkitUI.tools: List[Tool], has no from __future__ import annotations, and ExchangeToolkit.get_definition(cls) has no return type.
findings.impact: Documented types standard unmet in a newly added module; not enforced by the configured ruff rules.
findings.recommendation: Add from __future__ import annotations, use list[Tool], and annotate get_definition(cls) -> ExchangeToolkitUI.

findings.title: Migration baseline test is tautological
findings.problem: broken-verification-gap: PRE is loaded (line 47) from fa14587c0de1._ENUM_VALUES_FOLDED and test_pre_matches_down_revision_enum_values asserts PRE == that same attribute, so it cannot fail; test_migration_declares_expected_revision_chain only compares literal revision strings. Nothing asserts the Alembic chain has a single head at 5189d4d2afaf, and PRE is pinned to a file other than the actual down_revision u2v3w4x5y6a7. PRE is correct today (u2v3w4x5y6a7 does not touch credentialtypes), but nothing keeps it correct.
findings.impact: Consumer: the Alembic startup upgrade chain. A concurrent migration revising u2v3w4x5y6a7 (the fork this branch already hit, commit 562707199) yields two heads and `alembic upgrade head` fails at startup; a later credentialtypes change could make this migration's hardcoded list drop or re-add labels — and every test in the module would still pass.
findings.recommendation: Load the Alembic ScriptDirectory for src/external/alembic and assert len(script.get_heads()) == 1 and the head is 5189d4d2afaf; replace the self-comparison with an assertion of the migration's hardcoded upgrade/downgrade lists against the most recent credentialtypes sync_enum_values in the chain.
